title: The shared fake DOM becomes the one in fact: move the hand-written client test fakes onto it, with a census (LIN-4252 tidy-after)
description:
## Goal

The shared fake DOM (`tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`, LIN-4252) is the one fake DOM for client unit tests in fact, not only in CLAUDE.md: the hand-written copies are moved onto it and deleted, and a guard stops new ones.

## Context

LIN-4252 built the shared fake and moved two suites onto it. Two independent blind reads of that merge scored it "mixed" for the same reason: it owns 2 of about 30 consumers. 18 suites still hand-write a `makeContainer` (the eight `prompt-section-*` suites, `lin-3833/3968/3975/4016/4040/4042`, `scan-retire-ui`, `brief-recap-*`), and about 10 more carry their own `FakeElement`/`FakeClassList` (`chat-*`, `observation-*`, `flight-companion-client`, `lin-2933`, `lin-4035`). CLAUDE.md's "don't hand-write a `makeContainer`" has no guard behind it. "A helper that callers may adopt later is one more copy": this is that ticket's tidy-after.

## This step

Move the hand-written fakes onto the shared helper (and its vm layer, if LIN-4246 lifted one), deleting each copy in the same change. Add a census, beside `test-server-listen-bind.test.js`, that fails on a new hand-written fake DOM. While any copy remains, it's a ratchet with a count that may only fall. In pieces, by family, each green with unchanged test names. Stop at a family that doesn't pay, and say why.

**Not this ticket:** removing `prompt-section.js`'s `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards (production code).

## Done when

* The census is in `npm run test:unit`, and the count of hand-written fakes is as low as it paid to get it, ideally zero.
* Every moved suite keeps its test names and counts. Any test that goes red on a real DOM is reported as a finding, not loosened silently.

## Report back

Families moved, families stopped and why, findings, and the census count before and after.

## How to go about it (pruned at close-out)

The pre-work Survey (two comments, 12:26-12:27Z, at `b53917365`) is discharged: its census-first order and per-family pieces were carried out as the approved plan. Full text is in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

## At merge (who else must learn about it)

* The census is in `npm run test:unit`, and its list is shorter than the baseline. Give before and after.
* The fake's header lists its consumers and its "not modelled" lines, both current.
* CLAUDE.md names the census, within its byte budget.
* Every moved suite keeps its test names and counts, with the assertion map in the PR.

## Implementation Plan

Implemented as approved, with the course changes recorded in the final report (comment `4345cad0`, section 7): the consumer list was added to the fake header (`eba5537b`), the shared helper became `client-world.js`, non-layout APIs were allowed into the fake by team ruling (`abb313d9`), and `prompt-section-task-mode` and `lin-4016-browser-follows-server` went opposite ways to the plan (PR #2302, ruling `4a2a2dce`). Landed as LinearViewer PRs #2297-#2313 ([https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2313](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2313>) is the last); census 56 -> 25, 31 files moved, 9 stopped, 16 not attempted and dropped from this ticket (plan-review note 1b), now tracked in LIN-4254. The full plan, the Survey and the pre-prune description are preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

### Does it fit one session? `needs multiple sessions`

Six pieces, each its own PR. plan-review due: yes (more than one session, and it adds a guard whose definition is the design).

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4255 @ b53917365

LinearViewer `origin/main`. I counted 18 `makeContainer` definitions and 10 `FakeElement`/`FakeClassList` suites (11 with `lin-4035`). `createFakeDom` has 2 consumers besides its own test (`lin-4242`, and `lin-4010` via `loadWorld`). `loadWorld` (LIN-4246's vm layer) exists, and `lin-4246` uses it.

**Why it's hard**

1. **"~30 consumers" is two jobs, and the helper says no to the second one.** The `fake-dom.js` header lists as *deliberately not modelled* `id` and `className` as properties, event dispatch, and `getBoundingClientRect`. CLAUDE.md scopes the helper to `prompt-section.js`/`question-cards.js`. The `FakeElement` suites load other clients, and those use exactly these APIs: `className` (observation 34, flight-companion 19, chat 15), `style` (live-console 10), `scrollTop/Height` (flight-companion 9, live-console 6), `getBoundingClientRect` (live-console 3), `dispatchEvent` and `insertAdjacentHTML` (common/observation). Moving them means reversing LIN-4252's design choices and growing `fake-dom.test.js` to match. That's widening the helper, not a move. My forecast: the `makeContainer` family pays, and the `FakeElement` family is where it stops.

2. **The `makeContainer` fakes aren't trees.** They regex-splice an `_html` string, and `querySelector` answers only the slots each suite chose. Everything else returns `null` (`.swipe-prompt-options` is null on purpose), and `contains()` always returns true. On a real tree, every `container.querySelector ? … : null` branch in `prompt-section.js` gets a real element, so code paths these 18 suites never ran start running: the question-card keep, focus restore and swipe options. Expect reds. They're findings, maybe real bugs the fake hid. Budget for triage.

3. **Some assertions measure the fake itself.** `_fullRenders`/`_html`/`_clickHandler` appear 84 times across 10 suites (`prompt-section-go` 15, `-p0` 14, `-run-quota` 14, `-runner-link` 12, `lin-4040` 10). "Exactly one full render" has no meaning on a real DOM. Each one has to be re-expressed, for example as node identity kept across a partial repaint, or a spy on the `innerHTML` setter. Test names stay the same but the bodies change. Silent loosening slips in there, so the PR should map each old assertion to its replacement.

4. **The real serializer is stricter.** Valueless attributes serialize as `disabled=""`, entities are escaped, and the parser throws on malformed markup. Regexes written against the fake's raw string (`/disabled>/`, unescaped text) will break even when the behaviour is identical.

5. **The census is a definition problem.** A regex for `function makeContainer|class FakeElement` is beaten by renaming to `makeHost`. 66 suites carry ad-hoc `querySelector` stubs, mostly harmless `document` shims in the 116 vm suites. The census needs a rule that catches "an object pretending to be an element tree" without flagging `getElementById: () => null`. That rule is the real design work; `test-server-listen-bind.test.js`'s comment-stripping scan is a good template.

**What I'd do first**

Write the census before moving anything. Pin its definition, record the baseline count (my estimate is about 28), and make it a ratchet. Then move one hard `prompt-section` suite, `prompt-section-go` (30 tests, 15 fake-internal references, a click shim), onto `loadWorld`. It shows whether `_fullRenders` has a clean real-DOM equivalent and how many reds the null-guards hid, which prices the other 17. Move the `brief-recap`/`scan-retire`/`lin-*` suites with no fake-internal references next. Decide on the `FakeElement` family separately, as "widen the helper or stop", in writing.

## Survey global: LIN-4255 @ b53917365

**Where it lands.** `tests/unit`, with two layers already in place. `helpers/fake-dom.js` (728 lines: tree, parser, selectors) is the DOM. `helpers/prompt-section-world.js` (`loadWorld`) is the vm over it. LIN-4246 did lift it. Each layer has 2 consumers. The direction is right, but copies are still growing: LIN-4247 (b5cc4c62) added 106 lines of tests to `prompt-section-go`'s hand-written `replaceGoSlot` fake four minutes after LIN-4252 merged.

**Census at BASE:** 20 files define `makeContainer`, not 18 (`lin-3833` is two suites). 18 of the 20 also build their own `vm.createContext`, which is a second copy of what `loadWorld` already owns. Your loose `class Fake*`/`makeEl` grep finds 18 more files, but only about 10 of them fake a DOM (`chat-*` ×3, `observation-*` ×3, `flight-companion-client`, `lin-2933`, `task-chat-…-sentinel-mask`, `chart-helpers`). With 43 suites stubbing `createElement` and 117 using `vm`, "a hand-written fake DOM" needs a precise definition first.

**Done the obvious way, by family:**
- **prompt-section (13 suites) → `loadWorld`.** Good fit; each move deletes two copies (container and sandbox). Expect reds: these fakes match selectors as strings (`innerHTML.includes(attr)`), so a test can pass against them while being wrong on a real tree. Those reds are findings. `lin-4016` reads `<select>`/`<option selected>`, and the fake explicitly does not model `select`. Grow the fake or stop there.
- **brief/recap/scan (3 suites)** load `brief.js`/`recap.js`/`scan.js`. `loadWorld` says it is generic, but its file name and CLAUDE.md:58 tie it to prompt-section. Moving these suites without renaming leaves the name misleading.
- **FakeElement (chat/observation/flight-companion).** The header says it "deliberately does not model `id` and `className` as properties". `chat.js`, `observation.js` and `flight-companion.js` use `className` 18, 36 and 26 times. This family can't move without growing the fake. `scrollTop`/`scrollHeight` in `chat-tool-rows` are layout, but an expando on a real node covers them.

Lists that would have to learn about this, and nothing notices if they don't:
- the consumer list in fake-dom's header
- its "Deliberately not modelled" list
- CLAUDE.md:58, which should point at the census the way it points at `test-server-listen-bind.test.js`

`fake-dom.test.js` must test every addition.

**Better at a cost this task can carry:**
1. Rename `prompt-section-world.js` to a client-world name now, while it has only 2 consumers.
2. Add `className`/`id` reflection to the fake, with its own tests. Small, browser-faithful, unblocks the largest stopped family.
3. Have the census name files, not just a count. A ratchet keyed by count passes if one copy is deleted and another added. Copy the frozen-list ratchet in `workspace-token-eviction-census.test.js` and its siblings.
4. Move the prompt-section family first.

**Better still, not this task's:**
- `prompt-section.js` has 7 `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards that exist only to handle these fakes. Once the fakes are gone they're dead code. That's a follow-up, as the ticket says.
- The deeper cause is that every ticket's witness becomes a new `lin-NNNN` file with its own scaffolding. The census treats the symptom; the cure is a world helper that is the easiest thing to reach for.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The plan builds what was asked: a structural, file-list ratchet first, then family moves with an assertion map and a stop rule. Each gap I found is caught by a check the plan already has, so these are notes for the builder.

**What I checked, at `b5391736` (origin/main; nothing in `tests/unit/helpers`, `public/prompt-section.js` or CLAUDE.md has changed since).**
- The `test:unit` globs, and `acorn`/`acorn-walk` in `package.json`.
- CLAUDE.md is at 110 lines and 11,723 bytes against caps of 110 and 12,000 (`claude-md-line-budget.test.js:28-29`), so the plan's +277-byte budget is right.
- `prompt-section-world.js` has exactly 2 importers, plus CLAUDE.md:58.
- `loadWorld` already provides `container.click(dataset)`, and its scripts list is generic.
- The 18 `makeContainer` suites match the Survey.
- I wrote a rough acorn version of the plan's census rule (querySelector[All] plus one tree member, or three tree members, counted per object or class) and ran it over `tests/**` and the other two globs. All 18 `makeContainer` suites are caught. No parse errors. The world helper, `fake-dom.test.js` and `routing-fakes.js` are not caught.

**Notes for the builder**

1. **Expect a baseline of about 50, not about 28–30.** My prototype caught **54 files**. The extra ~24 are small element stand-ins with canned answers, such as `{ querySelector: () => countEl, classList }` (`dashboard-routes.test.js:6878`, `lin-4242-waiting-live:137`) and `{ parentNode, querySelector, querySelectorAll }` cards (`lin-4114-*`, `lin-4241-settled-ruling-client`, `question-card-task-bound`). Others in this group: `task-page-*`, `close-out-client`, `common-*-filter-nav`, `run-limit-gating`, `runner-link-surfaces`, `lin-4024-*`, `lin-3254`, `lin-3136-settings-take-predicate`, `lin-2122`, `lin-2370`, `lin-3975-proposal-refresh`, `lin-4016-sessions-fold-parked` and `observation-waiting-block`. They do fit "an object pretending to be an element tree", and the plan already says such files are listed as found, not trimmed. So:
   - (a) Do not tune the member list to bring the count down toward the Survey's estimate. Only change it through the in-test fixtures.
   - (b) None of the six pieces covers these files. The final report should put **every** listed file in one of three groups: moved, stopped (with the API that stopped it), or not attempted. Otherwise "as low as it paid" can't be checked.
   - (c) The census now blocks any new single-element stub in any client witness. Its failure message should say how to vm-run a slice against `createFakeDom()`'s `document`, not only how to use `loadWorld`.
2. **As written, the rule misses two Survey-named `FakeElement` suites.** The plan's cross-check ("a Survey file the rule misses means the rule is wrong") will flag them. Here is what to fix:
   - `chart-helpers.test.js:23`: its class defines `children` and `appendChild` (2 tree members) plus `replaceChildren` and `replaceWith`. Adding `replaceChildren` and `replaceWith` to the tree list catches it.
   - `chat-render-markdown-text.test.js:49`: it defines `classList` and an `innerHTML` getter/setter and is returned by a `document.createElement` stub. A structural signal that catches it: a class or factory returned from a `createElement` stub, with two or more tree members. Add both as positive fixtures.
3. **Don't import `stripComments` from `test-server-listen-bind.test.js`.** That file registers its `describe` at the top level (line 137). Importing it re-runs those tests inside the census process and changes the census suite's test count. acorn already drops comments, so the helper isn't needed. If a regex fallback ever needs it, move it into `tests/unit/helpers/` first.
4. **Piece 5, `lin-4016`: the plan's reading is half right, so expect the stop.** The test does find the selected `<option>` by regex, but it does so to hand back a **`.value` getter/setter** for the `<select>` (`lin-4016-browser-follows-server.test.js:23-41`). The client writes and reads that value: `prompt-section.js:1565` does `el.value = …` in `applyPanelDraft`, and `:2775-2784` reads `el.value` for `run-harness`/`run-effort`. The shared fake throws `value is not modelled on <select>` (`fake-dom.js:313`). The plan's own check ("if it needs `.value`, stop") settles it. The same throw will appear in **any** `prompt-section-*` suite that repaints the run-change panel with a draft. Record it as the `select` stop and as a fake artefact, not as a client bug.
5. **`tests/fixtures/observation-dom-shim.js` is a shared hand-written fake the Survey didn't name.** Its `FakeElement` has a full tree. The census will list it, and that is correct. Its consumers (`observation-scope`, `-waiting-block`, `-waiting-host`) define no fake of their own for it, so the census lists the fixture rather than them. Moving the observation family means deleting the fixture, which takes one entry off the list, not three.
6. **Census pattern source.** `workspace-token-eviction-census.test.js` pins a **count** (`KNOWN_DESTROY_COUNT = 5`), not a list of names. Use it only for the style of the failure message, as the plan does. The two-way set difference on a sorted name list is new to this file, and it is the right design.
7. **Piece 2.** The rename also changes CLAUDE.md:58 (8 bytes shorter). Do it in the same PR as piece 1's edit to that line, so the byte arithmetic is done once.

No blocking findings.

### Breakdown

I re-checked the plan against the code. LinearViewer `origin/main` is still `b5391736`, the plan's grounding SHA. Since this ticket was created (11:14Z), nothing has changed under `tests/unit/helpers/`, `public/prompt-section.js`, CLAUDE.md, `fake-dom.test.js` or `prompt-section-go.test.js`. The suites named in the plan match the files on disk, and CLAUDE.md is still 11,723 bytes. The plan has not drifted, so I broke it down as written. Each subtask carries its slice of the approved plan, cites the approving review (comment `98a20bc0…`, rev 1), and names `b5391736` as its grounding commit.

| # | Subtask | Plan piece | Blocked by | Session fit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | LIN-4265: census (structural, frozen file list) + rename `prompt-section-world.js` to `client-world.js` | 1 + 2 | none | one session. The plan allows one PR, and review note 7 asks for it so the CLAUDE.md:58 bytes are counted once. |
| 2 | LIN-4266: `prompt-section-go` pricing probe | 3 | LIN-4265 | one session. It is a single suite and acts as the gate for the family. |
| 3 | LIN-4267: `prompt-section-p0` / `-run-quota` / `-runner-link` | 4a | LIN-4266 | one session. Three suites, as the plan's "one PR per two or three suites" says. |
| 4 | LIN-4268: `prompt-section-preserve` / `-task-mode` / `-recommend-url` / `-look-alike` | 4b | LIN-4266 | one session. These are the lighter suites. |
| 5 | LIN-4269: `lin-3833`×2 / `3968` / `3975` / `4016` / `4040` / `4042` / `brief-recap`×2 / `scan-retire-ui` | 5 | LIN-4265, LIN-4266 | one session. The `lin-4016` stop on `<select>.value` is expected (review note 4). |
| 6 | LIN-4270: grow the fake with `className` and `id` reflection | 6A | LIN-4265 | one session. It touches only the fake and its tests. |
| 7 | LIN-4271: the FakeElement family, with the stop rule | 6B | LIN-4270 | **not claimed.** It is left for a fresh `plan` pass, which may split it by sub-family. |
| 8 | LIN-4272: close-out | report back + named out-of-scope items | LIN-4267, 4268, 4269, 4271 | one session |

**Choices I made, with the reasons**
- **Pieces 1 and 2 are one subtask.** The plan says one PR is fine, and review note 7 asks for the rename in the same PR as the CLAUDE.md:58 edit.
- **Piece 4 is two subtasks.** The plan already lands it as one PR per two or three suites. The 40 internal reads in `-p0`, `-run-quota` and `-runner-link` are too many to share a session with the four lighter suites. Both halves wait on the probe's gate.
- **Piece 5 waits on the probe (LIN-4266) as well as the rename.** `lin-4040`'s 10 internal reads use the replacement idioms and pricing the probe settles.
- **Piece 6 is split into A (LIN-4270) and B (LIN-4271).** The plan requires A to be green on its own before B starts. A depends only on the census, so it can run in parallel with the prompt-section moves ("the big move early").
- **I added a close-out subtask (LIN-4272).** Review note 1b found about 24 single-element stubs that the census will catch but no move piece covers. Without a final step that puts every listed file in one group (moved, stopped or not attempted), "as low as it paid" can't be checked. The close-out also files the follow-up for the 7 `container.querySelector ? … : null` guards and the world-helper cause. Because pieces 3–6 now land in parallel, the plan's "last piece's PR" no longer names one PR.
- **The review's builder notes are folded into the subtasks they affect:**
  - baseline of about 54, and no tuning toward the estimate: LIN-4265
  - the `replaceChildren`/`replaceWith` and `createElement`-factory rule fixes: LIN-4265
  - no `stripComments` import: LIN-4265
  - the `<select>.value` stop: LIN-4266, LIN-4267, LIN-4268, LIN-4269
  - `observation-dom-shim.js` as one census entry: LIN-4271

**LIN-4265 builder: one place the plan differs from the code (at `b5391736`)**

Pieces 1 and 2 and the review ("Done when": "The fake's header lists its consumers", and note 7) say that `tests/unit/helpers/fake-dom.js`'s header mentions `prompt-section-world.js` and lists the fake's consumers. **It does neither.** The header covers Modelled and Deliberately-not-modelled, and has no consumer list and no mention of the world helper. The only mentions of `prompt-section-world` were the 2 importers (`lin-4010` at lines 19 and 333, and `lin-4246` at line 19) and CLAUDE.md:58.

What I'm changing: the rename (commit `aa6ab081` on `feat/lin-4265-fake-dom-census-rename`, not pushed yet) has nothing to rename in `fake-dom.js`. The census beat of LIN-4265 will **add** a short consumer/guard section to that header, naming `client-world.js` (`loadWorld`) and the census. It will not edit an existing list. Later move pieces (LIN-4266 onward) will be adding to that new section, not to one that already exists.

Everything else checked out: there are no commits since 12:41Z on any of the paths involved, `loadWorld` is unchanged, and CLAUDE.md is now 110 lines and 11,715 bytes (8 bytes shorter, as note 7 predicted), so the census pointer has a budget of up to 285 bytes.

**LIN-4265 landed (PR #2297, `69e8f175`). Move-rule wording for the remaining pieces, accepted in review:** a moved suite **leaves** `HAND_WRITTEN_FAKE_DOM_FILES` and **joins** the `fake-dom.js` header's consumer list. The original text said "remove from both", which contradicts LIN-4255's "header lists its consumers, current". This applies to LIN-4266, LIN-4268, LIN-4269 and LIN-4271. The shared helper is now `tests/unit/helpers/client-world.js` (was `prompt-section-world.js`). Two frozen evidence snapshots under `docs/papers/harbour/task-size-and-cost-evidence/2026-11-05/` still quote the old name by design and must not be rewritten. The census baseline is 56 files, and each move piece shrinks it.

LIN-4266 (prompt-section-go, plan piece 3) fit in one session, across five beats. PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2299, CI green on eec8eb12.

Gate: the move was mostly mechanical. The non-mechanical parts were three presses that targeted controls production does not draw (the old stub never checked for the button), a task-surface setup that had to match the production gates, and the mutation proof. Measured: about 20 minutes from first to last beat dispatch, about 90 seconds per full unit-suite run, census baseline 56 to 55.

Recommendation: continue the prompt-section family, do not re-plan. The LIN-4268 suites are smaller (27 tests, about 880 lines) and mostly use _html and _clickHandler. Probe each one for presses on undrawn controls and for stubs that ignore their arguments before porting, since that is where this suite's cost was. The stop rule did not trigger. Not merged.

**Autopilot ruling on the prompt-section family gate (LIN-4266 landed: PR #2299, `56f9b474`, Tests run green on that commit).**

LIN-4266's review left the family decision to LIN-4255: the breakdown text said the family stops after the probe and is re-planned, while the PR's gate statement recommends continuing. Decision: **continue, as written, no re-plan.** Reason: the ticket's own stop rule is "stop when a family would need the shared fake widened beyond its current scope". The probe did not trigger it: no new fake API was needed, the move fit one session (about 20 min across five beats), and the suite's 30 test names/count are unchanged. The costs it found were in the old stubs (presses on controls production never draws, stubs that ignore their arguments), not in the helper.

For LIN-4267, LIN-4268 and LIN-4269: before porting each suite, check for presses on undrawn controls and stubs that ignore their arguments (that is where LIN-4266's cost was). If a suite genuinely needs an API the shared fake does not model (`getBoundingClientRect`, `style`, scroll, `<select>.value`), that suite stops and is reported with the reason; it does not widen the fake. Also from the LIN-4266 review: close-out confirms whether an AI-off disabled-next-step press test already exists (the R8 `btn.disabled` guard) and files a follow-up only if none does.

Releasing LIN-4267, LIN-4268, LIN-4269 now.

**Course-change note from the LIN-4271 plan (piece 6, step B), at `473cc865`.** The approved plan says "Widening the fake to make every family fit" is set aside, and only `className`/`id` reflection (LIN-4270, merged) is in scope. LIN-4271's pricing shows that wording would leave most of the FakeElement family on the census for reasons that are not stops. I'm changing course for this family and asking you to accept it.

**Why the plan is wrong here.** The stop rule's own text names four stops: `style`, `getBoundingClientRect`, scroll beyond a plain expando, and real event dispatch/bubbling. Of 17 suites, only `flight-companion-client` hits one (`style` plus layout read-back: `public/flight-companion.js:653`, `:662-665`). Nine more need only small, browser-faithful, non-layout APIs the fake lacks. `document.getElementById` is on all nine lists, and for four of them (`observation-card-order`, `-scope`, `-waiting-host`, `-waiting-block`) it is the only addition. I re-ran three of those four with just that one method added, and each passes with its spec output identical to the original; without it they go red (7 of 8, 3 of 3, 4 of 4). The other five need more: attribute-prefix selectors, `append`, `replaceChild`, `insertAdjacentHTML`, and so on. The ticket's own prediction that `live-console` stops did not reproduce: I ran both suites against a patched copy of the fake in the scratchpad and measured V8 coverage. 28/28 and 12/12 pass with names unchanged, and none of the `style`, `getBoundingClientRect` or `scrollTop` lines (`public/live-console.js:338-340`, `:703`, `:780`, `:925-927` and the rest) executes.

**What I'm proposing for the shared fake** (each with its own `fake-dom.test.js` case that fails on a no-op fake, header updated, one first PR before any move): `document.getElementById`; `[attr^=]`/`$=`/`*=` selector operators; `replaceChild`; `insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend')` only (other positions throw); the `·` entity; `replaceChildren` and `createElementNS`; `append`/`prepend`, `firstElementChild`/`lastElementChild`. **Not** proposed, and still stops: `style`, `getBoundingClientRect`, scroll beyond an expando, event dispatch/bubbling, `<select>`/`<option>` `.value` (one `observation-ruling-delivery` test uses it; that test gets a test-local accessor on its own element).

**This differs from your 14:22Z ruling**, which tells LIN-4267/4268/4269 that a suite needing an unmodelled API "stops and is reported; it does not widen the fake". I am not touching that: those three siblings proceed as ruled and none of them needs any of the APIs above, so there is no overlap in the fake. LIN-4266 added nothing to the fake (header only). LIN-4270 is Done; LIN-4272 waits on 4271.
